what: Tencent Music runs China's largest music streaming services, QQ Music, Kugou and Kuwo, and also operates live-streaming apps where listeners tip performers.
customers: Chinese listeners paying monthly subscriptions, and advertisers reaching them.
money: subscriptions, advertising and digital album sales
live-streaming rooms and karaoke, funded by virtual gifts
moat: Licences to the catalogues of the major record labels in China, plus a user base large enough that a rival paying the same licence fees cannot spread them as thinly.
risks: Chinese regulators have intervened in both music licensing and live-streaming before
The social entertainment half has been shrinking for years as regulation tightened on tipping
A Chinese company listed in New York carries delisting and disclosure risk
opportunities: 10.7 times earnings and 8.3 times free cash flow, cheap for a business with a 33.6% net margin
Paying subscribers and revenue per subscriber have both been rising, which lifted revenue back to $4.9B
Analysts see about 37% upside, with 28 covering the stock
watch: Paying subscriber count and revenue per paying user in the music segment.
